_about: Catalogue of everything script.js can contain. Read by `python tools/shorts.py guide` (for any AI model or person) and by `lint` (to catch unknown types and missing fields). Keep it in step with short.html.

safe_zones_px.note: Second-hand figures (platform ad templates relayed by third parties). 'organic' is the default; use safe:'strict' for paid ads. Check against a real upload.

script_keys.brand: handle shown at the top when there is no logo
script_keys.logo: image file in the project folder, shown instead of brand (omit to use the brand's logo; null = no logo)
script_keys.look: omit = the brand in brand.js if `brand` was run, otherwise 'clean'. Or force 'clean' | 'dark' | 'warm' | 'brand'
script_keys.theme: { accent:'#hex', dark:'#hex', bg:'#hex', secondary:'#hex' } recolours any look (brand.js sets this for you)
script_keys.captionStyle: 'stroke' | 'scrim' (omit for the default shadow); use over busy backdrops or footage
script_keys.syncWords: true = caption key words pop when spoken (needs words.js and captions in the voice's language)
script_keys.audio: voiceover file; its length sets the video length
script_keys.duration: seconds; only needed when there is no voice
script_keys.presenter: talking-head clip in the project folder, or null
script_keys.presenterOffset: seconds to skip at the start of the presenter clip
script_keys.backdrops: [{ src, t, end, zoom, pan, focus, dim, blur, fadeIn, fadeOut }] image/video files, or built-in backgrounds [{ style:'white' | 'sky' | 'night' | 'brand' | 'paper', t, end, ink:'dark' | 'light' }]
script_keys.moves: presenter only, needs a matte: [{ t, end, mode:'anchor', scale:0.6, side:'right'|'left'|'center' }, { t, mode:'punch', amount:0.12 }]
script_keys.captions: { style:'pill' | 'outline' | 'bold' | 'word', words:4, pos:'low' | 'mid' | 'split' } spoken captions built from words.js, each word turning solid as it is said ('word' = one word at a time); only when captions are in the voice's language
script_keys.splitCard: { left, top, width, height, radius } where the presenter card sits during split scenes (default: bottom third)

timing.seg: n or [n, m]: spoken line(s) from segments.js (written by `segments`)
timing.word: 'text' or ['text', nth]: start when this word is spoken, from words.js (written by `align`)
timing.rule: A scene runs until the next scene in its lane. Captions (cap, title) are one lane; every other type is the visual lane. Any visual may carry cap:{ lead, key, hl }.

cap.use: the spoken idea in 2-5 bold words
cap.notes: pos: 'top' | 'mid' | 'low'. hl:true = accent box, for the one word that matters.

bignum.use: one number or date that carries the point
bignum.notes: badges: source names as chips. Counts up when value is a number.

stat.use: one key fact on a dark card

compare.notes: layout:'stack' (rows, default for 3+ items or when bar is set) | 'side'. bar: 0-100, or true to size it from the value. win:true outlines the winner.

chart.notes: dir:'v' columns (up to 4) | 'h' rows (default for 5+, max 6). Real values only; name the source in note.

line.notes: 3-8 points, one series; only the first and last values are labelled.

dosdonts.notes: 3 short phrases per side, verbs first.

pills.use: who it is for / not for

list.notes: 3-5 items. at:[seconds] puts each row on its narrated beat.

quote.use: a sentence from an official source

web.use: the source page with the sentence highlighted

photo.notes: style:'polaroid' | 'card'. items:[{src, caption}] for a 2-3 photo collage.

kinetic.use: big words that carry the message on their own (product-film style)
kinetic.notes: 2-4 words. *word* = accent colour, _word_ = italic. pos:'top'|'low', align:'left'.

phone.use: a 3D phone that rises into frame, optionally with notification cards flying in
phone.notes: screen: image/video file of the app; or call:{name,status} for a built-in call screen. notes: up to 6 cards.

orb.use: a glowing orb for an assistant / AI / signal, with a label or a chip
orb.notes: at/to: [x,y] in px, the orb drifts between them. Best on backdrop style 'night' or 'brand'.

glass.use: a short checklist or feature list on a glass card
glass.notes: 3-5 items. exit:'zoom' flies through the card into the next scene.

screen.use: a screen recording or screenshot floating in 3D, turning and zooming to what matters
screen.notes: tilt/to: [rotY,rotX] degrees. spot:{x,y,w,h,at} in % of the picture.

mindmap.use: a framework drawn node by node on paper while the camera follows (creator-explainer style)
mindmap.notes: kind:'oval' (default) | 'plain' | 'hand' (big handwritten centre word). cam:[{at,x,y,zoom}] camera moves; end on a zoomed-out move that shows the whole map. glow:[{id,at,for}].

stickies.use: sticky notes popping up (goals, examples, a messy to-do list)

tags.use: 2-3 key words in hand-drawn ovals, appearing as each is said

headline.use: an editorial title in the top third, above the presenter's head; optionally a question that types on
headline.notes: title 1-3 words (*word* / _word_ work). body: one sentence, under 110 characters.

orbit.use: many examples around one idea: tiles on a turning ring, the idea lands in the middle

skeleton.use: 'here is what it looks like in a script': a document as grey bars, one line highlighted and explained, or real sentences typed and grouped
skeleton.notes: lines: a number, or a list of numbers (bars) and strings (sentences). marks:[{line,color,at}]. callout:{title,text,tags,at}. bracket:{from,to,label,at}.

picklist.use: a numbered list where one item is the point

formats.data explainer: voiceover + bold captions + charts, comparisons, sources (cap, bignum, chart, compare, ring, line, timeline, web, quote). Example: projects/shorts-reference
formats.product film: no presenter, little or no voice: kinetic type, 3D phone, cards, orb, glass card; the background changes with the story (white -> sky -> night -> white), 12-20 s. Example: projects/shorts-kinetic-reference
formats.creator explainer: a presenter intercut with full-screen graphics: mindmap on paper, stickies, tags, screen recordings, spoken captions (captions:{style:'pill'}), 30-60 s
formats.story b-roll: full-screen footage or generated clips (broll / backdrops) with small spoken captions (captions:{style:'outline'}), then presenter or screen scenes
formats.split explainer: a presenter in a card at the bottom, a black panel above with a section title (head) and a diagram that builds (orbit, skeleton, picklist, line, phone, chart...), one-word captions between them (captions:{style:'word',pos:'split'}); cut to the full-screen presenter between sections. Give every panel scene split:true. 45-90 s
